speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and potential bone fragility; please tell me, have you noticed any specific fractures from minor injuries or a general feeling that your bones break easily?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (specifically 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency).

The combination of ambiguous genitalia (labial fusion, clitoromegaly), delayed puberty (no menarche), and signs of hypertension/hyperandrogenism (severe acne, maternal hirsutism) points to this condition. I will order a plasma steroid profile and electrolytes to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Plasma_Aldosterone, Renin, Cortisol, 17-OHP, Testosterone, DHEA-S.
